Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

depictr (development version)

Upgrading from the previous release (0.3.0)

Changed results

  • Confidence intervals for a glm whose dispersion is estimated (Gaussian, Gamma, inverse Gaussian and quasi families) use the t distribution, as summary.glm() does, where they used z and were too narrow. They widen wherever depictr reports or draws them.
  • coefficient_plot(standardise = TRUE), and so model_report(), scales continuous inputs by their standard deviation and an interaction through its continuous inputs, leaving factor, logical and two-valued inputs unscaled (Gelman, 2008), where it scaled every model-matrix column, so a contrast depended on group balance.
  • coefficient_plot(standardise = TRUE) leaves poly(), ns() and other matrix terms unscaled, with a message, and warns about an interaction of continuous inputs that are not all centred. The axis and panel titles say which inputs were scaled.
  • coefficient_plot() reads an unnamed labels vector in model order, whatever order is, where it matched the vector to the terms as reversed or sorted for display, so a vector written for 0.3.0 can put labels on other terms. Named labels are unaffected.
  • model_fit_table() and the model_report() subtitle give every glm the deviance R², where they applied McFadden’s ratio to every family and could refit the null model on other rows. Binary logistic values change only where that refit went wrong.
  • model_fit_table() takes the AIC, BIC and log-likelihood of an lme4::lmer() REML fit from a maximum-likelihood refit, with a message, where it reported REML criteria, which cannot be compared between models with different fixed effects.
  • vif_plot() computes VIFs from the coefficients’ covariance, as car::vif() does, where it ignored the fit’s weights. Values change for a weighted lm, a binomial or Poisson glm and any other glm that weights its observations unequally. A model without an intercept changes too, with a warning.
  • tidy_estimates() exponentiates the estimates and limits of an lm, a glm, an lme4 fit and a data frame when given exponentiate = TRUE, where it ignored the argument for these and returned the link scale.
  • effects_plot(), interaction_plot() and model_report() build the prediction grid from the raw variables, so predict() re-applies every transformation, where a transformed term beside its raw variable gave a flat effect line or coincident interaction lines.
  • calibration_plot() and the Q-Q panel of residual_diagnostics_plot() pair each outcome of a glm fitted with na.action = na.exclude with its own fitted value, where they paired it with another row’s.
  • residual_diagnostics_plot() and influence_plot() leave out the rows that na.action = na.exclude excludes, for an lm as for a glm, without the warning they gave, and the 2p/n leverage line of influence_plot() no longer counts them.
  • The Q-Q panel of residual_diagnostics_plot() scales the quantile residuals of a weighted Gaussian or Gamma model by its prior weights, which it ignored, and leaves out observations with zero prior weight.
  • binned_residual_plot() and the binned panel of residual_diagnostics_plot() draw the band from the fitted model, where the empirical band was too narrow in bins without events, and leave out observations with zero prior weight. binned_residual_plot(band = "empirical"), though not the panel, restores the old band.
  • model_report() draws binned-residual and quantile-residual panels for a glm, as residual_diagnostics_plot() does, where it drew normal-theory panels that flag a correct logistic model. glm_panels = FALSE restores the old panels, and seed fixes the randomised residuals.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() and posterior_plot() keep only the b_ parameters of a posterior draws object that has them, as one made from a brms fit does, with a message, where frequentist_bayesian_plot() drew the group-level effects as parameters and pooled b_Intercept with Intercept.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() and posterior_plot() leave out the group-level effects of a stanreg fit and the log densities lp__ and lprior of any draws, which they drew as parameters.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() with draws plots only the terms both inputs share, with a message naming those it drops, where sigma and terms without a posterior took rows of their own, and sets the outer posterior interval by conf_level, where it stayed at 95%.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() reads a brms::fixef() matrix as a summary, where it drew the matrix’s four columns as parameters.
  • survival_plot() draws log-log confidence limits by default (Borgan & Liestøl, 1990), where it drew untransformed Greenwood limits. Unless time is a survfit object, conf_type = "plain" restores them, apart from the last step of a curve that falls to zero. conf_type = "log" gives the default of survival::survfit().
  • survival_plot() recomputes a survfit object’s limits at conf_level and conf_type, where it copied the object’s own and ignored conf_level. conf_type = "log" restores the limits of an object made with the defaults of survfit().
  • survival_plot() draws limits for a survfit object made with conf.type = "none", where it drew none. conf_level = NA leaves them out. An object without standard errors, or with Peto or modified lower limits, keeps its own and warns when they differ from those asked for.
  • survival_plot() reads the status coding once over all observations, where it read each group separately and so drew a group whose subjects are all censored under the 1/2 coding falling to zero. That group’s curve now stays at one.
  • survival_plot() honours group and status, as a column name or a vector, when time is a data frame, where it read them only from conventionally named columns and could pool the groups.
  • The number-at-risk table of survival_plot() counts a subject followed up to exactly a break and keeps a last break equal to the longest follow-up, both of which a floating-point error in the default breaks left out.
  • The median guides of survival_plot() follow survival::quantile.survfit(), where a rounding error could label the wrong time, a survfit curve flat at 0.5 could take its midpoint from a censoring time and a curve that ends at 0.5 got no guide.
  • Unless time is a survfit object, the confidence band of survival_plot() reaches the last event of a curve that falls to zero, where it stopped one event early.
  • k_diagnostic() and cluster_plot() default to k_range = NULL, which searches 1:8 for the gap and elbow criteria. The old 2:8 let the gap statistic find clusters in pure noise and kept the elbow from suggesting two. k_range = 2:8 restores it.
  • silhouette_plot() keeps the cluster labels it is given in its bands and in its "silhouette" table, whose cluster and neighbor columns are factors of them, where it recoded them to 1, 2, 3 and so on and gave neighbor as integer codes.
  • ts_forecast() and the forecast overlay of timeseries_plot() forecast the seasonally adjusted series with a random walk with drift, as forecast::stlf(method = "rwdrift", s.window = "periodic") does, where they extrapolated the last cycle’s trend with intervals far too narrow. The overlay caption names the method.
  • timeseries_plot() continues a forecast along the history’s own axis, numeric or Date, where it restarted near the start of the axis, and sorts an unsorted time before forecasting.
  • timeseries_plot() centres the moving average of an even rolling window, as a 2×12 average for rolling = 12 (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, 2021), where the average was drawn half an observation early. Odd windows are unchanged.
  • timeseries_plot() draws one line per column of a multivariate ts or a matrix, where it joined the columns into one series.
  • summary_table() summarises a date or date-time column as one Range row and a duration as mean (SD) in a unit that the statistic names, where it gave one row per distinct value.
  • palette_safety() and check_figure() measure colour separability with CIEDE2000 (Sharma, Wu & Dalal, 2005), where the 1976 distance overstated the differences between saturated colours, so distances and some verdicts change. metric = "cie76" restores the old measure.
  • simulate_cvd() at partial severity interpolates between the published matrices of Machado et al. (2009), where it drew the full-severity matrix towards the identity, so its colours between severities 0 and 1 change. Full severity is unchanged.
  • check_figure() measures each text against its own background, holds large text to 3:1 and measures a translucent plot or panel background as the colour it shows, where it measured all text against the plot background at 4.5:1.
  • check_figure() composites translucent colours over their background with the alpha each geom applies, where it measured them as opaque, and compares colours and fill colours each among themselves, where it pooled them, so verdicts can change in either direction.
  • check_figure() counts a colour or fill split across layers, one value per layer, as a colour encoding, where it reported none, and counts shape and line type split that way towards redundant_encoding.
  • check_figure() adds a tenth row, annotation_text_size, which holds the text inside the panel, such as annotations, geom_text() labels and the cell values of depictr’s plots, to the size floor, so a figure that passed can fail.

Changed interface

  • depictr requires ggplot2 3.5.2 or later, where it declared 3.5.0, with which the current patchwork cannot load, and suggests lme4 1.1-19 or later.
  • coefficient_plot(), timeseries_plot() and decompose_plot() take new arguments before title, palette and confidence respectively, so those arguments and the ones after them must be passed by name.
  • tidy_estimates(), save_plot(), frequentist_bayesian_plot(), scale_colour_depictr() and scale_fill_depictr() take a new argument before ..., so an argument meant for ... must be passed by name.
  • A conf_level outside (0, 1), such as 95, is refused by every function that takes one, where a level of 0 or 1 gave the model estimates zero-width or unbounded intervals, 95 gave missing intervals or an error and roc_curve_plot() without ci ignored the level. Without ci, roc_curve_plot() also refuses NULL, which it ignored.
  • Every function that takes a conf_level, except survival_plot() and calibration_plot(), refuses NA, where most gave missing intervals. Those two still take it to leave the limits out, and both refuse NaN, which they read as NA.
  • compare_models() and frequentist_bayesian_plot() read an unnamed labels vector as one label per term, in the order the terms first appear, where they took one label per row of the stacked estimates or per posterior draw, and refuse a vector of the old length.
  • For a posterior draws object that holds b_ parameters, frequentist_bayesian_plot() and posterior_plot() take labels keys without the prefix, so a key such as b_rainfall written for 0.3.0 no longer matches.
  • survival_plot() refuses a factor, character or non-integer status, which it read by its level codes, as missing or truncated to an integer.
  • survival_plot() refuses a status coded 0/1 in some groups and 1/2 in others, which it read group by group.
  • survival_plot() refuses a group or status name that matches no column of a data frame time, which it ignored.
  • effects_plot(), interaction_plot() and model_report() refuse a formula term computed from statistics of its rows, such as I(x - mean(x)), which shifted the line, a formula that reads columns with $ and a transformed term whose data the call cannot supply.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() with draws refuses inputs that share no terms and two terms of either input that would share a label, and posterior_plot() refuses a brms::fixef() matrix and two parameters that would share a label.
  • explore_distribution(), ecdf_plot(), raincloud_plot(), group_comparison_plot(), explore_categorical(), explore_pairs(), ridgeline_plot() and outlier_plot() refuse a numeric group with more than 20 distinct values, which they drew, and scatter_trend() refuses one when called, where it returned a plot that failed when drawn.
  • scatter_trend(), explore_distribution(), ecdf_plot(), raincloud_plot(), explore_categorical() and outlier_plot() refuse a group missing for every row when called, where they drew it or returned a plot that failed when drawn.
  • power_curve_plot() refuses rows of one curve that share a sample size, where it joined them into a zigzag line.
  • acf_plot(), decompose_plot(), seasonal_plot() and ts_forecast() refuse a series of more than one column, and timeseries_plot() refuses a forecast for one, where they joined the columns into one series.
  • timeseries_plot() refuses an even rolling window as long as the shortest series, since the centred average spans one observation more than the window.
  • pca_plot() refuses a misspelt group column, a group vector of the wrong length and a column name passed with a prcomp object, which it read as one level or padded with NA.

Changed output

  • coefficient_plot(), compare_models(), frequentist_bayesian_plot(), optimizer_fixef_plot() and the coefficient panel of model_report() label a two-level factor or logical input with its level, as in treatment: enhanced, where they showed treatment. Except in model_report(), labels = c(treatmentenhanced = "treatment") restores an old label.
  • In an interaction row, the same functions name the variable and level of every factor, as in rainfall × treatment: enhanced, where they showed rainfall × treatmentenhanced. Except in model_report(), a labels entry for the raw term restores it.
  • compare_models() labels the factor levels of every model, as in region: South, where it labelled only those of the first model holding a factor and showed the rest as regionSouth. A labels entry for the raw term restores them.
  • compare_models(x_lab = NULL), and frequentist_bayesian_plot(x_lab = NULL) with summaries, draw the default axis title, ‘Estimate’ or the ratio’s name, where they drew none. Adding ggplot2::labs(x = NULL) removes it.
  • The model_report() subtitle of a glm calls its R² ‘deviance R²’, where it said ‘pseudo-R²’.
  • estimation_plot() and group_comparison_plot(differences = TRUE) give every group a column in the difference panel, the reference’s first and empty, so each difference sits in its own group’s column, where the difference panel had one column fewer than the groups and spread across the full width.
  • The caption of estimation_plot() and group_comparison_plot(differences = TRUE) writes a round number of resamples in full, as 100,000, where it printed 1e+05.
  • group_comparison_plot(differences = TRUE) keeps each group’s colour whatever the reference, where the colours moved between groups, and estimation_plot() matches a named palette to the levels by name.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() draws the frequentist estimates in brand blue and the Bayesian ones in orange on both paths, where the draws path swapped them, and adds a caption naming each source’s interval level. caption = NA omits it.
  • save_plot() writes PDF, EPS and PostScript files with the cairo devices, which embed the fonts, and a TIFF LZW-compressed on white unless bg is given, where the files failed journals’ checks. device = "pdf", "eps", "ps" or "tiff" restores ggplot2’s devices.
  • save_plot() rasterises the translucent layers of an EPS or PostScript file at 600 dpi or more, with a message, where it left them out.
  • Without cairo, as on a Mac without XQuartz, save_plot() writes a PDF, EPS or PostScript file with a message or warning saying what the file lacks, and a Mac with neither XQuartz nor ragg writes the TIFF uncompressed, with a warning.
  • seasonal_plot(style = "season") draws its cycle lines from a ramp that starts at #4a8fc0, at 3.51:1 against white, where the earliest cycles were close to invisible. palette = depictr_palette(n, type = "sequential"), with n the number of cycles, restores the old ramp.
  • palette_preview(), confusion_matrix_plot() and correlation_heatmap() draw each label in black or white, whichever contrasts more with its tile, where some labels fell below the 4.5:1 that WCAG asks of text.
  • pca_plot() fixes the aspect ratio, so a figure of another shape gains blank space, and draws its loading arrows and labels in dark grey, where they took the accent, the palette’s fourth colour.
  • Without group, power_curve_plot() draws one curve per level of an effect, param or term column, with a message, where it joined them into one line.
  • power_curve_plot() draws a confidence band from <power>_lo and <power>_hi columns, such as the power_lo and power_hi of a pilotr sweep over sample size, where it drew none, and reads them before lower and upper.
  • scatter_trend(), explore_distribution(), ecdf_plot(), raincloud_plot(), group_comparison_plot(), explore_categorical(), explore_pairs(), ridgeline_plot() and outlier_plot() drop rows with a missing group, with a message, and give no colour to a level without rows, so the colours of the levels after it can shift.
  • ridgeline_plot() keeps each ridge’s colour when an earlier group is too sparse to draw, where the later ridges shifted colour. group_comparison_plot() and raincloud_plot() leave a level without rows off the axis, where they kept an empty place for it with a warning.
  • explore_distribution() and ecdf_plot() draw a numeric group code, such as blocks numbered 1 and 2, as groups, where they drew one ungrouped curve.
  • explore_categorical() orders its groups by level, where it sorted them alphabetically.
  • With the default palette, scatter_trend(), explore_distribution(), ecdf_plot(), raincloud_plot(), group_comparison_plot(), explore_categorical(), ridgeline_plot() and outlier_plot() warn once past eight groups, when the plot is made, where they warned each time the plot was drawn.
  • The caption of a grouped timeseries_plot() names the average of an even rolling window as, for example, ‘2×12 centred moving average’, where it said ‘12-point’.
  • timeseries_plot() keeps the level order of a factor group, where it ordered the groups by first appearance, and leaves out unused levels, so the legend order and colours can change.
  • decompose_plot(method = "classical") leaves out missing values at either end of a series, so its panels start at the first observation and end at the last, where they spanned the missing stretch.
  • explore_bivariate() treats dates, date-times and durations as numeric, where it took them for categories, so they give a scatter plot with a trend or box plots by level.
  • threshold_plot() draws its metrics as steps that change at each score, where it joined adjacent scores with straight lines.
  • dumbbell_plot(sort = "none") keeps a factor’s level order, or else the order in which the categories first appear, where it sorted them alphabetically.
  • survival_plot() drops an arm whose every status is missing, also when group is a factor, where it kept it in the legend with no curve and made logrank = TRUE fail.
  • The text_contrast row of check_figure() reports the text furthest short of its own threshold, with that threshold and the text’s printed size and weight, and a translucent colour is named with its alpha.
  • The colour rows of check_figure() say when colour is a continuous scale, which they do not audit, where they said that nothing was distinguished by colour.
  • The separability rows of check_figure() say whether their closest pair are colours or fill colours, and its text_size and text_contrast rows no longer say that a figure draws no text when all of its text is inside the panel.
  • On ggplot2 3.5.x, pca_plot() and silhouette_plot() draw their labels without a border or a warning about linewidth, as on later versions.
  • citation("depictr") gives the DOI that CRAN registered, https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.depictr, where it gave the Zenodo concept DOI, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21266308.

New features

  • simulate_figure() shows a finished ggplot or patchwork, legend and colourbar included, as a reader with a colour-vision deficiency sees it, and returns a gtable to draw or save.
  • depictr_palette(order = "contrast"), also in scale_colour_depictr() and scale_fill_depictr(), reorders the palette so that up to three groups pass every colour check of check_figure() and four keep 3:1 against white. depictr_options(palette = ) can make it the default.
  • exponentiate = TRUE in coefficient_plot() and compare_models() gives odds, rate or risk ratios, which the plots draw on a log axis with the reference line at 1 and an axis title naming the ratio.
  • check_figure() audits a patchwork composite, the package’s own included, panel by panel, with a leading panel column, where it refused one.
  • check_figure(max_text_pt = ) checks a ceiling on text size in a text_size_max row, and save_plot(check = TRUE) audits a figure at the width it is saved at, gives one warning that names each failed check and attaches the report as attr(, "check").
  • power_curve_plot(solved = ) marks a solved sample size, such as the result of pilotr’s target_n(), with a dashed line and its interval as a grey band.
  • power_curve_plot() reads the output of pilotr’s power_curve_mixed() as it is, with its n_subject column and its band, and gains n, power, group, lower, upper and y_lab after its existing arguments. Several curves are told apart by colour and line type.
  • coefficient_plot(standardise = TRUE, sd_multiple = 2) scales continuous inputs by two standard deviations, Gelman’s (2008) convention.
  • ts_forecast() and timeseries_plot() gain lambda, for a Box-Cox or log transformation, and decompose_plot() gains s_window, the STL seasonal window.

Minor improvements

  • posterior_plot() and frequentist_bayesian_plot() format each parameter’s label once, and format_terms() is much faster on long vectors, so a draws object with many draws no longer takes minutes to plot.
  • pca_plot() takes an unquoted group column name and refuses a prcomp fit that holds no scores, with a message that says so.
  • vif_plot() refuses a model with aliased coefficients and names their terms, where it failed with an unrelated base-R error.
  • correlation_heatmap() refuses a column in cols that it cannot correlate, such as a factor or a date, and names it, where it failed with an error that did not.
  • explore_pairs() refuses a numeric group named in cols with a message that says so, where it failed with an error from cor().
  • decompose_plot() and ts_forecast() refuse a missing value inside the series with a message that names x, and a series of exactly two cycles gets the package’s own message.

Fixes

  • estimation_plot() and group_comparison_plot(differences = TRUE) work in a fresh R session, where they failed unless patchwork had been loaded.
  • effects_plot(), interaction_plot() and model_report() work with a transformed term, such as log(), poly() or ns(), and with an offset, held at its mean on the link scale, where they failed. A name such as "log(rainfall)" stands for the variable it transforms.
  • random_effects_plot() draws models with several uncorrelated or split random-effect terms per grouping factor, such as (1 + x || g), fitted with lmer() or glmer(), where it failed.
  • A glm fitted with na.action = na.exclude works in the ROC, precision-recall, threshold, gain and lift plots and in confusion_matrix_plot(), which failed.
  • posterior_plot() reads a posterior draws object made from a brms fit, on which it failed with an error about duplicated factor levels.
  • posterior_plot() accepts an unnamed labels vector with one label per parameter, which it refused.
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() with summaries no longer warns about labels keys it was not given.
  • ts_forecast(), the forecast overlay of timeseries_plot() and decompose_plot() with its default STL method read a one-column ts and trim missing values at either end of a series, where the STL decomposition failed. A forecast starts after the last observation.
  • seasonal_plot() accepts a frequency that is not a whole number, such as 365.25 / 7, and rounds it down to whole seasons with a message, where it refused every such frequency.
  • scatter_trend() accepts a numeric group code, which failed with a discrete-scale error.
  • explore_pairs() leaves a numeric group out of its default columns, where it failed with an error from cor().
  • On ggplot2 3.5.x, the reference lines of coefficient_plot(), frequentist_bayesian_plot() and posterior_plot() no longer warn about an unknown inherit.aes.

Deprecated

  • metric = "cie76" in palette_safety() and check_figure(), kept to reproduce colour distances computed before this release. The default, "ciede2000", replaces it, and a later release will remove it.

Documentation

  • The README and the help pages of depictr_palette(), depictr_options() and palette_safety() no longer call the built-in palette the Okabe-Ito set. The help page of depictr_palette() says that it keeps six of that set’s eight colours, with the brand blue and a grey in place of its blue and black.
  • The README points to the Python README’s list of the differences between the twins, where it said that they differ in a few places.
  • Help pages that described behaviour the code does not have now match it. explore_pairs() refuses columns beyond max_cols, posterior_plot() refuses an unknown style and depictr_palette(n = NULL) gives seven colours for a ramp. depictr_options() and theme_depictr() no longer present depictr_brand(), depictr_accent() and depictr_reference() as functions to call, since the package does not export them. cluster_plot(seed = NULL) draws from the session’s random-number stream, coefficient_plot() applies interaction to the terms a named labels vector leaves out and survival_plot() tests a survfit object with the base-R log-rank test. missingness_map() takes its missing-cell colour from the accent, k_diagnostic() takes the elbow farthest from the chord, dumbbell_plot() puts the shortest dumbbell at the top only when every difference is negative and estimation_plot() no longer says that zero lines up with the reference group’s mean.
  • vignette("exploring-data") says that summary_table() takes its column names as strings and that an argument naming several columns, such as cols, takes a character vector, where it said that column names could be given quoted or unquoted. It also says that, of the model-estimate plots, only coefficient_plot() takes standardise and that every plotting function returns a ggplot, where it said that all of them took standardise and that every function returned a ggplot. vignette("model-estimates") and the help page of coefficient_plot() no longer claim that standardised magnitudes are comparable. The help page of threshold_plot() and vignette("diagnostics-and-uncertainty") say that the maximum-F1 threshold is drawn dotted and the Youden threshold dashed, where they said both were dashed. vignette("multivariate-and-survival") says that only an arm whose curve reaches 0.5 gets a median guide, and vignette("time-series") says that STL holds the seasonal component fixed under the default s_window = "periodic", where it said that STL lets it change from year to year.
  • The help page of check_figure() gains a section on auditing a figure at the width it is printed at, with the text floors of four publishers, where it called 6 pt a common publisher floor, and says that four colours of the default palette fall below 3:1 against white. The help page of save_plot() describes the formats that three publishers accept.
  • vignette("depictr") shows a figure drawn by simulate_figure() and covers four publishers’ text floors, Nature’s ceiling, the contrast-first palette order and how the audit treats a continuous colour scale.

depictr 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-01

Auditing a finished figure

  • New check_figure(), an accessibility and honesty audit of the figure you are about to submit. Until now the package could vouch for its palette and say nothing about a finished plot, which is the thing a reader sees. Give it anything a depictr function returns, including a plot extended afterwards with +, and it introspects the build and returns a tidy table. The rows cover the separability of the encoding colours under each dichromacy and in greyscale, the smallest text size against a stated physical output width, the WCAG contrast of the text and of the geometry against their backgrounds, and whether any distinction is carried by colour alone. Every row carries the value it measured beside the threshold it was measured against, so a verdict can be argued with.
  • The colour-vision helpers are exported. simulate_cvd() and palette_safety() were internal here while the Python twin exported both, so the advertised parity did not hold. They now match in name, arguments, return shape and refusal wording. simulate_cvd() gains a severity argument and returns lower-case hex, as the Python twin does. palette_safety() returns the full report, naming the worst condition, the closest pair and the verdict. The old return was a bare vector of distances.
  • The accessibility claim has been narrowed to what is true. The default eight-colour palette clears every colour-vision check and fails the new greyscale check: its orange (#e69f00) and sky blue (#56b4e9) differ by 0.79 in CIE lightness, so a black-and-white printer renders them as the same grey. The Okabe-Ito guarantee is about hue confusion and was never a claim about greyscale. The threshold stays where it is, and vignette("depictr") now states the limitation where the claim is made, so the package’s own defaults are held to the same standard as anybody else’s.

Figures that misreported the data

  • quantile_residuals() produced nonsense for a cbind(successes, failures) binomial model. The two-column response matrix was flattened to a vector and the raw success counts were then multiplied by the trial totals a second time, so the residuals of a well-specified model centred far from zero and the Q-Q diagnostic looked catastrophically misspecified. The matrix response now supplies its counts and trial totals directly, and the residuals are standard normal again where they should be.
  • ridgeline_plot() stacked its overlaps upside down. The row sort meant to draw the top ridge first is a no-op, because ggplot2 draws ribbon groups in factor-level order, so each upper ridge painted over the one below it, the opposite of the conventional ridgeline overlap. The draw order is now carried by the group aesthetic, with the colour assignment unchanged.
  • random_effects_plot(sort = TRUE) froze every facet in the first facet’s order. With more than one term the level factor was shared across panels, so only the first panel came out sorted and the rest zigzagged. Each facet now orders its own levels, with the plain level names kept on the axis.
  • A user-supplied title in power_curve_plot() is no longer run through format_terms(), which turned a colon into a multiplication sign and blanked underscores. Only a title recovered from the power-curve object, which is a raw term name, is tidied.
  • survival_plot() drew a phantom arm for a group that does not exist. An NA in group became a level of its own, matching no observation, so the plot gained an all-censored curve for a group nobody was in, and under logrank = TRUE it failed outright. Missing groups are now dropped with a message saying how many.
  • survival_plot() silently discarded non-finite follow-up times. Dropping a case from a Kaplan-Meier fit changes the denominator, and so every step of the curve and every cell of the number-at-risk table, while the figure carries no trace of it. It now refuses them, with the same message as the Python twin, since whether to drop or impute is the analyst’s decision to make. This replaces a silent drop, so it is a behaviour change for anyone who relied on the old handling.
  • depictr_palette() interpolated past its accessibility guarantee without saying so. Beyond the eight Okabe-Ito base colours the palette is a ramp, and the colour-vision-deficiency guarantee that is this package’s reason for existing stops holding, so the interpolated palette fails the package’s own safety check. It now warns at the point of interpolation, and only for the built-in palette, since a user-supplied one carries no such claim. The documentation is qualified to match.
  • summary_table() counted missing-group records in Overall and in no group column, so the per-group sizes silently fell short of the headline N. They now get a Missing column of their own.
  • A seeded plot leaked its seed into the caller’s random stream in a session that had not yet drawn a random number, so the documented reproducibility guarantee quietly failed in exactly the fresh session that would rely on it.
  • compare_models(facet = TRUE) now honours depictr_options(reference = ) for its per-panel reference line. seasonal_plot() no longer labels a frequency-7 series Mon..Sun, an alignment a plain ts cannot know. And a mistyped labels key now warns, so the raw parameter name no longer sits on the plot.

Degenerate input

  • survival_plot() now says when it drops observations with a missing status, in the wording of the missing-group message. The drop was previously silent. A status that is missing for every observation is an error. This brings the third kind of incomplete survival input into line with the other two, a missing group being announced and a non-finite time refused.
  • silhouette_plot() checks that clusters has one entry per row of data before dropping incomplete rows. A vector sized to the complete rows used to slip past the late check, because subsetting it with the logical index padded it with NA, and then died in the distance computation. It is now refused with the same message cluster_plot() uses.
  • tidy_estimates() no longer fails on a rank-deficient lm with a raw “differing number of rows” error. confint() keeps aliased terms as NA rows while coef(summary()) drops them, so the intervals are now cut to the estimated terms, with a message naming the aliased terms that were left out.
  • cluster_plot() and k_diagnostic() drop zero-variance columns with a message when scale = TRUE, as correlation_heatmap() already did, so a raw k-means error no longer escapes. k_diagnostic() now names the values of k_range it cannot evaluate instead of dropping them from the search without a word, and explore_pairs() labels an undefined correlation n/a where it once printed r = NA beside a raw stats::cor() warning.

Metadata and documentation

  • The declared minimum dependency versions are now installed and tested by a CI job. The patchwork floor is raised from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0. That was verified by running it: 1.2.0 cannot run model_report() at all, because patchwork::free(type =, side =) arrived in 1.3.0.
  • gain_plot() documents that the perfect-model reference line is drawn for a single model only, which is what the code has always done, and a test now pins it. The line bends at the prevalence of the outcome, and overlaid models need not share a prevalence.
  • model_fit_table() documents that a single model is enough, which is what the code always accepted, and raincloud_plot() no longer claims to be built from base graphics primitives: like ridgeline_plot(), it is base R and ggplot2 alone.
  • ?depictr again lists every exported function (scale_fill_depictr() and the scale_color_depictr() alias were missing), the README no longer describes the Python package as a feature-parity twin (its own README says otherwise), CONTRIBUTING no longer claims the maintenance workflows close their own issues, and the standardise = TRUE axis label now names the x-only convention the figure uses.
  • The README no longer opens with a link to the documentation site, which on the site’s own home page pointed the reader at the page in front of them.
  • Every vignette now turns console colour off and fixes the console width while it renders. pkgdown passes the calling terminal’s colour support into its build subprocess, so a coloured message or error would otherwise reach the reader as escape sequences in the middle of the text.

depictr 0.2.2

Examples that match the chart

  • The precision-recall, gain and lift examples move to an outcome with a scarce positive class, which is the case those charts are documented for. They previously ran on an outcome that was 94 per cent positive, so the gain curve sat on the diagonal and lift hovered at one.
  • The calibration example fits a model and plots its predicted probabilities, since a reliability curve is a check on a fitted model.
  • The power-curve article names the effect the shipped simulation actually covers, and its no-simr branch reads a summary derived from that simulation, so the two branches agree by construction.

Fixes

  • vif_plot() restricts its scale to the severity levels present, which removes an empty key entry from the rendered figure.

depictr 0.2.1

Documentation

  • The introductory vignette shows depictr_palette() returning the palette’s hex colours directly, ready for scale_fill_manual() or a base-graphics col = argument, and shows depictr_options() setting defaults for every later plot and returning the previous values, so the earlier look can be put back afterwards.
  • vignette("diagnostics-and-uncertainty") saves an arranged panel with save_plot(), which writes at a print-ready 300 dpi by default and creates any missing directories.
  • vignette("multivariate-and-survival") adds k_diagnostic(method = "gap"), which compares within-cluster dispersion against a null reference and so, unlike the other two criteria, can support k = 1.
  • vignette("time-series") adds classical decomposition, which holds the seasonal component fixed across the series where STL lets it evolve from year to year.
  • The optimizer_fixef_plot() and power_curve_plot() reference pages describe what each plot shows. Both pages previously described the prototype gists the plots grew from.
  • On the documentation site, source chunks are set a little smaller than the output and the prose, so a typical line fits the narrower home and article columns without horizontal scrolling, and the copy button stays attached to its code block.

depictr 0.2.0

Fixes

  • roc_curve_plot() rejects a ci that resolves to fewer than one bootstrap resample, with a clear error. Until then it drew an all-NA band and an [NA, NA] AUC annotation, saying nothing.

Data

  • In wellbeing_survey, region now shifts stress and income, which flow through to life satisfaction. The region-grouped plots (faceted densities, ridgelines, the region dendrogram) therefore compare four distinct distributions where earlier they compared four samples of one. The bundled datasets are regenerated by data-raw/generate_datasets.R as before.

Citation

  • The package citation (inst/CITATION and CITATION.cff) carries the Zenodo concept DOI, and the citation title uses sentence case.

Documentation

  • The package overview (?depictr) lists every exported function and all five bundled datasets. Previously several functions and two datasets were missing.
  • The vif_plot() example fits deliberately collinear predictors, so the plot shows inflated VIFs sitting above the threshold line. The earlier example produced near-identical bars around 1, with the line off the axis.
  • depictr_options() describes what brand and accent actually drive, and depictr_palette() notes that qualitative colours interpolated beyond the base set are not guaranteed to stay distinguishable under colour-vision deficiency.
  • lift_plot() documents its own top-right inside-legend corner rather than inheriting gain_plot()‘s bottom-right wording, and DESCRIPTION notes that composite panels return ’patchwork’ objects.
  • References throughout the documentation follow APA 7 and carry DOIs, and spelling is consistently British (en-GB).
  • The documentation site’s home page is restructured around a pitch, gallery and signposts. The time-series decomposition example draws its trend confidence band. LICENSE.md carries the full MIT text so the site’s licence page renders in full, as in the sibling packages.

Packaging and checks

  • Example variants that render several multi-panel figures (posterior_plot(), residual_diagnostics_plot(), decompose_plot()) are wrapped in \donttest{} so each example file stays within CRAN’s five-second budget. The first call of every example still runs.
  • CITATION.cff and the test artefact Rplots.pdf are excluded from the build tarball, and the test that produced Rplots.pdf draws to a null device instead.
  • New tests pin the legend_inside gates. The legend moves inside the panel when a plot’s gate is satisfied, and the theme is left alone when it is not.

depictr 0.1.1

  • Documentation and packaging polish, with no change to the plotting API.
  • The documentation site adopts the shared house style used across the package family, with a citation page carrying a copyable and downloadable BibTeX entry.
  • Consolidated to a single LICENSE file, and added community and contribution files.

depictr 0.1.0

First release. depictr is a unified, consistent toolkit of publication-ready plots spanning the whole analysis workflow. It grew out of, and generalises, three earlier plotting functions (frequentist_bayesian_plot, plot.fixef.allFit and powercurvePlot).

Exploring data

  • explore_distribution(), explore_categorical(), explore_bivariate(), explore_pairs(), correlation_heatmap(), missingness_map(), outlier_plot(), raincloud_plot(), group_comparison_plot(), scatter_trend() and summary_table().
  • estimation_plot() for estimation statistics: group effect sizes (mean differences, Cohen’s d / Hedges’ g) with bootstrap confidence intervals, in the spirit of the ‘new statistics’.
  • ecdf_plot() (empirical cumulative distribution, optionally by group), ridgeline_plot() (overlapping per-group densities) and dumbbell_plot() (a connected two-group comparison across categories).
  • explore_distribution() gains facet to draw one panel per group instead of overlaying them (much clearer beyond a few groups), and correlation_heatmap() gains reorder to cluster correlated variables together.

Multivariate, clustering and survival

  • pca_plot() and scree_plot() (principal component analysis), cluster_plot() (k-means on principal-component axes) and dendrogram_plot() (hierarchical clustering), and survival_plot() (Kaplan-Meier curves with a number-at-risk table, median survival and an optional log-rank test, all computed in base R).
  • silhouette_plot() and k_diagnostic() help choose and validate the number of clusters (silhouette widths, plus elbow and average-silhouette diagnostics).

Time series

  • timeseries_plot() (one or more series with an optional moving average), acf_plot() (autocorrelation / partial autocorrelation) and decompose_plot() (trend / seasonal / remainder decomposition).
  • seasonal_plot() (seasonal subseries) and ts_forecast() (a simple, dependency-free forecast with prediction intervals).

Model estimates and inference

  • tidy_estimates() provides the shared tidy estimate table, with methods for lm, glm, merMod and data frames and a fallback to broom::tidy().
  • coefficient_plot(), compare_models(), frequentist_bayesian_plot(), effects_plot(), interaction_plot(), random_effects_plot(), optimizer_fixef_plot() and model_fit_table().
  • frequentist_bayesian_plot() now draws the full Bayesian posterior for each term as a half-eye density and overlays the matching frequentist point estimate and confidence interval, so the two inferential frameworks can be compared directly. It reads posterior draws from brmsfit, stanreg, draws/matrix objects or a data frame.

Diagnostics and classification

  • residual_diagnostics_plot(), influence_plot(), qq_plot(), vif_plot(), roc_curve_plot(), pr_curve_plot(), gain_plot(), lift_plot(), calibration_plot() and confusion_matrix_plot().
  • binned_residual_plot() (binned residuals for logistic and other GLMs, with approximate error bounds) and threshold_plot() (classification metrics across decision thresholds, highlighting Youden’s J and the maximum-F1 cut-off).

Uncertainty and power

  • posterior_plot() summarises posterior draws with a choice of styles ("halfeye", "interval", "gradient" or "dots") and can annotate a region of practical equivalence (ROPE) and the probability of direction.
  • power_curve_plot() for power-analysis curves (e.g. from simr).

Theming and reporting

  • theme_depictr(), depictr_palette(), scale_colour_depictr() (and scale_color_depictr(), scale_fill_depictr()), palette_preview(), format_terms(), model_report() (a one-figure model overview), arrange_plots() and save_plot().
  • depictr_options() sets package-wide defaults once, covering the brand and accent colours, qualitative palette, base font size and family, and the colour used for missing values. Every plot and scale then honours them.

Layout and legibility

  • coefficient_plot(), compare_models(), posterior_plot() and frequentist_bayesian_plot() gain a facet/scales option that lays each term out in its own free-scaled panel, so terms on very different scales (a large intercept alongside small slopes) stay legible instead of being squished onto the zero line. frequentist_bayesian_plot() uses this layout by default.
  • Every plot has had a pass for legibility. silhouette_plot() cluster labels no longer clip. raincloud_plot() uses one colour per group across all layers. dendrogram_plot() hides leaf labels for large trees. confusion_matrix_plot() picks each label’s colour from the tile luminance. gain_plot() and lift_plot() label their reference lines. timeseries_plot() shows a single legend, and k_diagnostic() now returns the diagnostic curve as a plot.
  • coefficient_plot() gains standardise, scaling each coefficient by its predictor’s standard deviation so magnitudes are comparable. model_report() uses it by default, removing the empty band in its coefficient panel.
  • vif_plot() shows the ordinary VIF (not its square root) for single-df terms, scales the axis to the data, and draws a single clearly-labelled threshold line (reported in the caption when it is off-axis), leaving no wide empty band or hard-to-read guides.
  • seasonal_plot(style = "season") reverses its sequential legend so the darkest, most-recent cycle sits at the top, matching the plotted order.
  • Factor coefficient names are prettified by default to the effect (variable) name in coefficient_plot(), compare_models() and frequentist_bayesian_plot(), where they are read from the model, so conditionunrelated becomes condition and word_frequency becomes word frequency. optimizer_fixef_plot() and posterior_plot() gain a labels argument for the same. Any user-supplied labels take precedence. pca_plot() likewise shows underscores in its loading-arrow labels as spaces (soil_ph -> soil ph).
  • Redundant cluster legends are dropped: silhouette_plot() (the bands are labelled in place) and cluster_plot() when the centroids are labelled.
  • survival_plot() has been tidied in several ways. The log-rank annotation renders a proper chi-squared and an italic p, formatted APA style (no leading zero, p < .001 below that threshold). The median guide is labelled median <value>. The y-axis title margin is tighter, and the colour legend and the number-at-risk table list the groups in the same order, following the group factor’s levels.
  • A legend_inside argument (off by default) draws the legend inside the panel, over a semi-transparent background, in a corner the plot usually leaves empty, which reclaims the right-hand margin. It is offered by roc_curve_plot(), gain_plot(), lift_plot() (bottom-right / top-right of the curve), ecdf_plot(), survival_plot(), explore_distribution(), dumbbell_plot() and missingness_map(). For any other plot the same is one theme() call, and vignette("exploring-data") shows how, alongside tidying legend titles.
  • theme_depictr() now centres legend titles over their keys, which reads more tidily than ggplot2’s default left alignment, especially for an inside or a top/bottom legend.
  • estimation_plot() reserves more headroom above the lower panel so the effect-size annotation (Hedges’ g / Cohen’s d) is never clipped.
  • scree_plot() colour-matches and names its dual axes, ‘Variance explained (bars)’ on the left and ‘Cumulative (line)’ on the right.
  • Statistical letters are italic in annotations: the log-rank p, model_report()’s n and R, and estimation_plot()’s g / d.
  • British (en-GB) spelling throughout: the crop_yield column is now fertiliser, coefficient_plot()/model_report() take standardise, and confusion_matrix_plot() takes normalise.

Data

  • Five reproducibly simulated datasets: lexical_decision (counterbalanced priming experiment), wellbeing_survey (with realistic missingness), crop_yield (a fertiliser-by-treatment field trial), clinical_trial (right-censored survival with a rare adverse event) and monthly_sales (two seasonal retail series).

Accessibility

  • The qualitative palette is based on the colourblind-safe Okabe-Ito set (led by the depictr brand blue), and depictr_palette() provides sequential and diverging variants. palette_preview() can show any one, or all three, and can simulate deuteranopia, protanopia or tritanopia so a palette’s legibility can be checked directly.

Notes

  • Heavier modelling back-ends (lme4, broom, simr, survival, brms, posterior, ggdist, cluster, boot) are in Suggests and used only when available, so the package installs and checks without them. Vignettes draw on small precomputed model fits shipped in inst/extdata/, so they knit without a Bayesian or mixed-model toolchain.
  • Functions with an optional seed (cluster_plot(), qq_plot() and residual_diagnostics_plot()) restore the caller’s random number generator state afterwards, so passing one for reproducibility has no side effect on your own subsequent random draws.
